summary: With χ = χ_K(p), write the e-th term as (c/(1 − χ))·(p^{−e} − (χ/p)^e) (the multiplier 2c/(1 − χ) times half the difference of the two geometric terms); it vanishes at e = 0. Sum the two geometric series in the two cases χ = −1 (multiplier c/2: the odd terms, sum cp/(p² − 1)) and χ = 0, p = d (multiplier c: all positive terms, sum c/(p − 1)).

steps.claim: Both geometric series converge (|1/p| < 1, |χ/p| < 1, χ = χ_K(p)); the convert matches the given sum with 2c/(1 − χ) times half their difference, so the e-th term to identify is (c/(1 − χ))·(p^{−e} − (χ/p)^e), which is 0 at e = 0. Since χ ≠ 1, χ = −1 or p = d with χ = 0: in the first case the term is (c/2)(1 − (−1)^e)p^{−e}, i.e. c/p^e for odd e and 0 for even e, and the odd terms sum to cp/(p² − 1) = c·(1/(p−1) − 1/(p²−1)) = (2/2)·c·(1/(p−1) − ρ_p); in the second the term is c/p^e for every e ≥ 1 (the multiplier is c, not c/2) and the sum is c/(p − 1) = 2c·(1/(p−1) − 1/(2(p−1))). The case split, `simp_all` and `grind` check these identities term by term and for the sums.
steps.lean:
convert! (((@hasSum_geometric_of_abs_lt_one p⁻¹ _).sub (@hasSum_geometric_of_abs_lt_one
  (chiK d p / p) _)).div_const 2).mul_left _ using 2 <;> obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨⟩⟩⟩ | _⟩ := chiK_cases d p,
  @Padic.norm_p_lt_one p <;>
  simp_all [nonsplitWeight, neg_one_pow_eq_ite, ↓div_pow, zero_pow_eq] <;> grind [NeZero.natCast_ne]
